current_episode.title: #56 - Navigating Senior Living: Compassionate Placement & Care Strategies with John Killeen

guest.bio_context: John Killeen has worked with the senior population for over 30 years, starting as a Director of Food Nutrition and then serving as Regional Director of Operations for a contract food service company where he managed 15 accounts across the Southeast. He became owner of his Oasis Senior Advisors franchise just under two years ago after exploring franchise opportunities with a consultant and deciding this business model aligned better with his goals than other options like home care franchises.

pending_qa.q: How many franchises operate nationwide and what geographic coverage does the franchise system provide?
pending_qa.r: Oasis Senior Advisors is a nationwide franchise with 120 owners throughout the country. While John Killeen primarily serves Pinellas County, the franchise network can connect families to communities in other states—for example, if someone in Pinellas needed to move to New York, the company could facilitate that relocation.

pending_qa.q: What experience did John Killeen bring from the food service industry to senior living placement?
pending_qa.r: John Killeen spent 30 years total in food service, including 15 years as a Regional Director of Operations managing accounts across the Southeast in assisted livings, memory cares, and independent living communities. This experience gave him deep awareness of operations, food service quality, and facility management across senior care environments.

pending_qa.q: How should families approach difficult conversations about transitioning seniors to assisted living facilities?
pending_qa.r: John Killeen recommends focusing conversations on safety concerns like falls and home clutter that could cause injury. He suggests scheduling tours proactively before a transition is needed, and framing assisted living positively by highlighting the extensive activities and social programs available, which he describes as making facilities feel like mini resorts rather than care institutions.

pending_qa.q: What flexibility exists in assisted living lease terms that families should know about?
pending_qa.r: Many assisted living communities have month-to-month lease options despite lengthy paperwork appearing to require a year-long commitment. Residents typically only need to provide 30 days notice to leave, giving families the option to try a placement and transition elsewhere if it does not work out.

pending_qa.q: What specific factors should families evaluate when touring senior care communities?
pending_qa.r: John Killeen advises families to observe staff interactions with residents and among themselves, sample the meals since seniors eat three meals daily there, and avoid asking salesperson-directed questions so they can see authentic responses. He emphasizes that no community is perfect, but these observations help identify whether an environment is genuinely conducive to resident wellbeing.

pending_qa.q: Why did John Killeen choose the Oasis Senior Advisors franchise over a home care company despite initially leaning that direction?
pending_qa.r: John Killeen decided that a home care franchise posed too much risk as a one-person operation because hourly employees are critical to quality, and one or two poor performers could ruin the business. He preferred Oasis because it allowed him to operate as a solo business owner while still having access to software, marketing materials, and established systems.

pending_qa.q: What marketing and operational systems does the Oasis franchise provide to support owners?
pending_qa.r: Oasis provides software tools including a CRM system and community database with photos and descriptions. The company creates monthly newsletters, weekly Facebook content adaptable to LinkedIn and Instagram, and supplies all marketing materials, so owners primarily enter information into the CRM and let the systems distribute content automatically.

pending_qa.q: How did John Killeen receive his initial opportunity to explore franchise ownership?
pending_qa.r: John Killeen received an unsolicited call from a franchise consultant who contacted him out of the blue without him making any inquiry. This unexpected call sparked his interest in exploring franchise opportunities and led him to work with the consultant to evaluate options.

pending_qa.q: What role did networking groups play in establishing John Killeen's visibility and referral network in Pinellas County?
pending_qa.r: John Killeen joined multiple networking organizations including the Seminole Business Alliance and Better for Living Seniors, where he built relationships and gave his 60-second pitch regularly. He credits this effort with raising his visibility over nearly two years so that referral partners from hospitals, rehabs, elder law offices, and home care companies now recognize him as an established, stable business partner.

pending_qa.q: What demographic trend in the United States is driving the need for senior placement and care services?
pending_qa.r: In the next 20 years, there will be 90 million people over the age of 65 in the United States. John Killeen emphasizes that this demographic shift requires dedicated professionals with empathy to provide quality care services for seniors, as current staffing shortages are already creating challenges that will worsen without intervention.

pending_qa.q: What is John Killeen's advice for someone considering purchasing a franchise?
pending_qa.r: John Killeen recommends doing thorough exploration with a franchise consultant who asks the right questions about interests, work schedule preferences, and investment capacity. He notes that all franchises have a seven-step evaluation process that allows candidates to exit at any stage if the fit does not feel right, so potential owners should complete as many steps as possible to confirm it is truly a good match.
